summary: The day is dominated by practical small-x and femtoscopy methodology rather than new experimental heavy-ion measurements. Key themes are CGC event generation for EIC saturation observables, unstable light-nucleus resonance extraction through partial-wave femtoscopy, collider-inference validation under nuisance shifts, and profile-likelihood bias in localized signal searches.
strongest_paper: 2609.03434: CGC-py is the strongest heavy-ion-adjacent contribution because it turns full CGC DIS kinematics into a validated event-generator workflow while giving a sober assessment of EIC saturation reach.

papers.title: CGC-py: A Monte Carlo Event Generator for Gluon Saturation Physics
papers.authors: Haowu Duan, Cong Yi, Si-Wei Dai, Shu-Yi Wei, Wenbin Zhao, Liang Zheng
papers.abstract: The authors develop CGC-py, a DIS event generator coupling the full CGC cross section for gamma*p(A) to a parton-branching TMD backward initial-state shower, with Pythia 8 handling final-state radiation and hadronization. The generator keeps target-elastic and target-inelastic contributions without the back-to-back limit, validates single-inclusive spectra analytically and against H1 ep charged-hadron data, and predicts modest but structured eAu saturation effects at EIC kinematics.

papers.title: A Practical Partial-Wave Method for Identifying Unstable Light Nucleus Resonances in Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.authors: Junlin Wu, Hongchan Li, Ke Mi, Yaping Wang, Guannan Xie
papers.abstract: This paper extends the Lednicky-Lyuboshitz femtoscopy framework to higher partial waves and uses low-energy scattering phase shifts to isolate resonance components in two-particle correlation functions. Demonstrations for p-3He and p-4He target the 4Li and 5Li ground-state resonances, producing correlation peaks consistent with known resonance parameters and spectra based on STAR 3 GeV proton/light-nuclei inputs.

papers.title: Measurement of the forward angle 12C+12C fragmentation differential cross sections at 62 MeV/nucleon
papers.authors: G. Guo, G. Casini, B. H. Sun, S. Barlini, A. Camaiani, C. Frosin, et al.
papers.abstract: This work reports high-precision forward-angle fragmentation differential cross sections for 12C+12C at 62 MeV/nucleon using the FAZIA array. It extracts angular distributions for fragments with Z=1 to 6, compares heavier-fragment distributions to Van Bibber and Goldhaber descriptions, and finds an anomalously narrow alpha distribution plausibly tied to intrinsic 12C clustering.

papers.title: Reduced latent leakage does not reliably predict lower likelihood bias in collider inference
papers.abstract: The paper tests whether reducing physics-label readability in a nuisance branch of reusable collider embeddings reliably reduces profiled signal-strength bias under unmodelled shifts. In CMS H->ZZ->4l and top-jet workflows, leakage reductions preserve task performance, but their association with maximum profiled bias is weak, and held-out confirmation sometimes increases bias.

papers.title: The Greedy Bump Bias: Local Profiling Geometry and the Look-Elsewhere Effect
papers.abstract: The work connects positive amplitude bias from profiling an unknown localized signal with the look-elsewhere effect through the geometry of a family of signal templates. It derives asymptotic relations in Gaussian matched-filter models and decomposes global bias into local profiling and remote-peak competition terms.

papers.title: Reconstruction of Shower-like Events in NEON Using Likelihood and Graph Neural Network Methods
papers.authors: Sujie Lin, Weiqin Huang, Yihan Liu, Chengyu Shao, Lili Yang, Huiming Zhang
papers.abstract: The paper builds a first shower-event reconstruction framework for the proposed NEON deep-sea neutrino telescope, comparing a calibrated maximum-likelihood pipeline with a two-stage graph neural network. Simulations report MLE angular resolution near 4.19 degrees and a GNN improvement to about 1.8 degrees at 30 TeV, with energy resolution around 20% in an intermediate range.

papers.title: TQ4Q2.0 Fragmentation Functions for Fully Heavy Tetraquark Production
papers.abstract: A compact proceedings update on collinear fragmentation functions for fully heavy tetraquark production, with NRQCD inputs, threshold evolution, fragmentation-scale uncertainties, and intrinsic-charm sensitivity at LHC/FCC energies.
